sources.title: Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency
sources.claim: Crypto returns exhibit strong time-series momentum and investor-attention predictability, supporting mechanism-first momentum/regime architectures rather than indicator-only crossovers.
sources.limitations: Broad crypto return evidence; not a direct executable BTC/ETH perpetual strategy or cost model.

sources.title: Intraday Return Predictability in the Cryptocurrency Markets: Momentum, Reversal, or Both
sources.authors: Zhuzhu Wen; Elie Bouri; Yahua Xu; Yang Zhao
sources.claim: Intraday crypto predictability changes with jumps, liquidity and event regimes, supporting explicit momentum-vs-reversal regime ownership instead of unconditional fading or chasing.
sources.limitations: Historical high-frequency study; execution costs and current exchange microstructure must be revalidated prospectively.

sources.title: Perpetual Futures and Basis Risk: Evidence from Cryptocurrency
sources.authors: Will Gornall; Juan Martin Rinaldi; Yizhou Xiao
sources.claim: Constrained arbitrage and speculative demand can create persistent futures-basis dislocations, motivating basis/funding/OI architectures tied to deviation and unwind mechanisms rather than raw funding thresholds.
sources.limitations: Mechanism evidence; exact BingX funding/basis/OI source and execution costs remain strategy-specific.

sources.title: High-Frequency Jump Analysis of the Bitcoin Market
sources.authors: Olivier Scaillet; Adrien Treccani; Christopher Trevisan
sources.claim: Order-flow imbalance, aggressive trading and spread widening predict Bitcoin jumps and jump impact can persist, so reversal systems should distinguish exhaustion from informed-flow continuation.
sources.limitations: Mt. Gox-era data; mechanism must be revalidated on current BingX data.

sources.title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
sources.authors: Rama Cont; Arseniy Kukanov; Sasha Stoikov
sources.claim: Short-horizon price changes are strongly related to order-flow imbalance and inversely to market depth, supporting entry-time flow/depth state as a causal microstructure variable.
sources.limitations: Equity-market study; crypto transferability requires prospective validation.

sources.title: Backtest overfitting - in-sample vs out-of-sample
sources.claim: Repeated redesign after observing scored PnL contaminates OOS; preserve a true holdout and bound redesign cycles.
sources.limitations: Community guidance, not primary alpha evidence; used only for research-process safeguards.

sources.title: Minimum viable holding period given transaction costs
sources.claim: Strategy frequency must be compatible with its natural signal horizon and transaction-cost budget; cost viability should influence which horizons are worth researching.
sources.limitations: Community discussion; used as architecture-screening rationale, not PASS evidence.

sources.title: To people currently running a live strategy - what's your next move?
sources.claim: Practitioner discussion emphasizes new uncorrelated strategies, execution-cost reduction and avoiding excessive retuning of profitable systems.
sources.limitations: Anecdotal practitioner discussion; hypothesis/error-mode source only.

sources.title: Order Flow Trading System v6
sources.claim: Community implementation explicitly conditions order-flow signals on trend/range/volatile/illiquid regimes, reinforcing regime-conditioned flow as a testable hypothesis rather than unconditional signal stacking.
sources.limitations: Community indicator with proxy order-flow components; not accepted as proof of profitability.

sources.title: Master Strategy: BTC W1 Mean Reversion [Institutional SOP]
sources.claim: Weekly-range sweep and reclaim provides a slower-horizon, larger-move mean-reversion architecture candidate that may offer better move-to-cost geometry than 5m scalp attempts.
sources.limitations: Community script; use only as architecture inspiration and reimplement independently with prospective validation.
